title: An Inverse Theorem for Extremal Generalized Narkiewicz Sequences over C₃³
headline: A Lean-verified inverse classification of extremal length-24 sequences in the three-dimensional group over the field of three elements.
description: For the three-dimensional group over the field of three elements, earlier work established a threshold of 25 terms for forcing two short zero-sum subsequences whose intersection has nonzero sum. This project proves the exact length-24 inverse theorem for nonzero entries: avoidance of such a pair holds if and only if the sequence is, up to a permutation of its original positions, three copies of eight distinct elements with no nonempty zero sum of length at most three. Both directions are formalised in Lean 4 and registered with Palomar. An illustrated manuscript and reproducible arXiv source package are prepared, but the repository records no arXiv posting or journal submission.
summary: The classification preserves the original positions of each term, so it is stronger than an analysis of the set of distinct values alone. The proof draws on published zero-sum thresholds, constructions and residual-sequence lemmas, with a new necessity argument constraining all possible extremal multiplicities. Its established scope is this particular group and length; the documented prior-art search is not a certification of worldwide novelty or priority.
verification: The exact two-direction positional classification is proved by InverseZeroSum.Candidate3.frozenClassification. Palomar Registry v1 records successful Lean kernel and independent NanoDa/con-ron checks of the pinned proof (mechanical verification run 37813245157); the repository's S062 Lean and manuscript-validation workflows also passed. These checks do not establish historical priority or journal publication.
attribution: John Fairfax-Ball is the named author and responsible maintainer. This project supplies the complete inverse necessity and equality argument building on published threshold, construction and residual-sequence results by Gao and collaborators (2024) and Fan and collaborators (2012); those earlier results are credited rather than claimed as new. Substantial OpenAI ChatGPT assistance contributed to mathematical exploration, proof construction, Lean formalisation, checking and documentation under the author's direction.
original_source: W. Gao, W. Hui, X. Li, Y. Li, Y. Qu and Q. Zhong, “On generalized Narkiewicz constants of finite abelian groups,” Acta Arithmetica 212(2) (2024), 133–172, DOI: 10.4064/aa230118-1-10 (known threshold, threefold construction and packing/deletion method). Y. Fan, W. Gao, G. Wang, Q. Zhong and J. Zhuang, “On Short Zero-Sum Subsequences of Zero-Sum Sequences,” Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 19(3) (2012), P31, DOI: 10.37236/2602 (short-free residual structure, including the proof of Lemma 27(3)).
